            if (-not $d.BirthAnchor) { continue }   # nothing of its own to mint from; leave it reported
            $newCid = (New-SIObjectUuidV5 -Name (Get-SILedgerKey -Type $d.BirthAnchor.Type -Value $d.BirthAnchor.Value)).ToString()
            if ($newCid -eq $k) { continue }

            # Re-point this half's OWN anchors at the new id. The contested anchor is already absent
            # from $d.Identifiers, so it stays with the keeper -- which is what stops the two halves
            # merging again on the next run.
            $rewritten = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]
            foreach ($id in @($d.Identifiers)) {
                [void]$rewritten.Add([pscustomobject]@{ Type = $id.Type; Value = $id.Value; CorrelationId = $newCid })
            }
            $d.NewIdentifiers = $rewritten.ToArray()
            $d.CorrelationId  = $newCid
            $d.Action         = 'split'

            [void]$splits.Add([pscustomobject]@{
                CorrelationId = $k; NewId = $newCid; Objects = $claimants.Count; Resolved = $true
                KeptBy = $keeper.CorrelationId; Kind = 'operator'
                Reason = 'an operator never-merge separated this object; the other half keeps the existing id and this half is a NEW object'
            })
        }
    }

    [pscustomobject]@{
        Decisions     = $decisions.ToArray()
        Superseded    = $superseded.ToArray()
        ShrunkObjects = $shrunk.ToArray()
        Splits        = $splits.ToArray()
        Minted        = @($decisions | Where-Object { $_.Action -eq 'mint'  }).Count
        Reused        = @($decisions | Where-Object { $_.Action -eq 'reuse' }).Count
        Merged        = @($decisions | Where-Object { $_.Action -eq 'merge' }).Count
        Split         = @($decisions | Where-Object { $_.Action -eq 'split' }).Count
        # #642 of them: the objects split off a ledger id that held another object as well (a wrong merge, repaired)
        WrongMergeSplit = @($splits | Where-Object { [string]$_.Kind -eq 'wrong-merge' }).Count
        Unkeyable     = $unkeyable
    }
}

# ---- identity/SI-ObjectLedgerStore.ps1 :: Save-SIObjectLedger
function Save-SIObjectLedger {
    <#
        Persist one run's decisions: new anchors, and any merge supersessions.

        🔒 ONE TRANSACTION. A half-written merge is the worst possible state -- anchors re-pointed at a
        survivor while the superseded row is missing means the connector never learns old -> new and
        orphans a CI, which is precisely the failure the ledger exists to prevent. All or nothing.

        Anchors are UPSERTed by (type, value), never blind-inserted: an anchor already present under
        the same id is the normal case on every run after the first, and must be a no-op rather than a
        primary-key violation.
    #>
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]$Connection,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][AllowEmptyCollection()][object[]]$Decisions,
        [Parameter()][AllowEmptyCollection()][object[]]$Superseded,
        [Parameter()][datetime]$Now = ([datetime]::UtcNow)
    )

    # EVERY ROW IS MADE READY AND CHECKED BEFORE THE FIRST ONE IS WRITTEN: a value longer than the column goes in as its
    # short form (ConvertTo-SILedgerStoredValue), and a row the table cannot hold is refused here, in a moment -- not by
    # the database after minutes of writes that are then all undone.
    $anchors = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]
    foreach ($d in @($Decisions)) {
        if ($null -eq $d -or [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([string]$d.CorrelationId)) { continue }
        foreach ($n in @($d.NewIdentifiers)) {
            if ($null -eq $n) { continue }
            $anchors.Add([pscustomobject]@{ Type = [string]$n.Type; Value = (ConvertTo-SILedgerStoredValue -Value ([string]$n.Value)); CorrelationId = [string]$n.CorrelationId })
        }
    }
    Assert-SILedgerRowsFit -Rows $anchors.ToArray()

    $tx = $Connection.BeginTransaction()
    try {
        $written = 0
        foreach ($n in $anchors) {
            $c = $Connection.CreateCommand(); $c.Transaction = $tx; $c.CommandTimeout = 120
            $c.CommandText = @'
MERGE si.ObjectIdentity AS t
USING (SELECT @ty AS IdentifierType, @va AS IdentifierValue) AS s
   ON t.IdentifierType = s.IdentifierType AND t.IdentifierValue = s.IdentifierValue
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET SI_CorrelationId = @cid, LastSeen = @now
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (IdentifierType, IdentifierValue, SI_CorrelationId, FirstSeen, LastSeen)
     VALUES (@ty, @va, @cid, @now, @now);
'@
            [void]$c.Parameters.AddWithValue('@ty',  [string]$n.Type)
            [void]$c.Parameters.AddWithValue('@va',  [string]$n.Value)
            [void]$c.Parameters.AddWithValue('@cid', [string]$n.CorrelationId)
            [void]$c.Parameters.AddWithValue('@now', $Now)
            [void]$c.ExecuteNonQuery()
            $written++
        }

        $sup = 0
        foreach ($s in @($Superseded)) {
            if ($null -eq $s) { continue }
            $c = $Connection.CreateCommand(); $c.Transaction = $tx; $c.CommandTimeout = 120
            $c.CommandText = @'
IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM si.ObjectIdentitySuperseded WHERE OldId = @old)
INSERT INTO si.ObjectIdentitySuperseded (OldId, NewId, SupersededAt, Reason)
VALUES (@old, @new, @now, @why);
'@
            [void]$c.Parameters.AddWithValue('@old', [string]$s.OldId)
            [void]$c.Parameters.AddWithValue('@new', [string]$s.NewId)
            [void]$c.Parameters.AddWithValue('@now', $Now)
            [void]$c.Parameters.AddWithValue('@why', 'merge: anchors resolved to two ids')
            [void]$c.ExecuteNonQuery()
            $sup++
        }

        $tx.Commit()
        [pscustomobject]@{ AnchorsWritten = $written; SupersededWritten = $sup }
    } catch {
        try { $tx.Rollback() } catch {}
        throw
    }
}
